title: The Place | Get Assistance Today
text:
Support.Empower.Transform.
To assist the people of Forsyth and Dawson County areas with essential needs and to be self-sustaining.
Who We Are
The Place is a local nonprofit serving Forsyth and Dawson counties, helping individuals and families meet essential needs such as food, clothing, and financial assistance while guiding them toward long-term self-sufficiency through education, workforce training, and holistic support.
Values
Compassion and Hope
We provide an inclusive and welcoming environment for all clients. We review each case on an individual basis and work to address all needs we identify.
Dignity and Respect
We evaluate all processes to focus on the dignity of those we serve. We demonstrate respect by listening to and offering support to our clients.
Accountability and Stewardship
We maintain the highest standards in the nonprofit and business world. We ensure all donations are used appropriately to accomplish the greatest good. We focus on sustainability and carrying out our mission with increased efficiency and effectiveness.
Collaboration and Coordination
We bring resources together to transform lives in our area. We seek to identify gaps of needs in our community and, through collaboration, find creative ways to meet the needs.

LOCATIONS AND HOURS
Forsyth location2550 The Place Circle, Cumming, GA 30040Monday through Saturday from 9:00am–4:00pm
Dawson location829 GA 9 North, Dawsonville, GA 30534Closed MondaysTuesday through Saturday from 9:00am–4:00pm
What to Wear and Bring
Closed-toed shoes, comfortable clothing, no tank tops and minimal jewelry. For your safety, sandals and flip flops cannot be worn in our warehouses. REQUIRES standing, bending and lifting items up to 25lbs.
If you would like to bring a lunch or a snack, we have a refrigerator and break room. Please bring water.
Please complete the application below. You will receive an email from our Volunteer Coordinator with next steps.
Interested in Group Volunteer Opportunities?
We provide group volunteer opportunities if your school, business, or church is looking to give back. The opportunities range from clothes sorting at our Thrift Store, shopping and packing non-perishables for client orders, or possibly even something a little different! If you or your group is interested, please email our Volunteer Coordinator, Amber Pham (amber@theplacega.org)
Ongoing Volunteer Opportunities
Thrift Store Volunteers at The Place thrift store work closely with the staff unloading donations, sorting and inspecting, hanging clothes, or organizing the retail floor. This is a great opportunity for individuals and groups to make a difference. Recurring and one-time volunteer opportunities are available.
Food PantryVolunteers at The Place Food Pantry are assisting in making sure our clients are receiving all of their orders when they arrive. We provide a high level of customer service by providing car side service. You might help to pack food bags, sort through baked goods, or help load groceries into vehicles. Individual opportunities available at the food pantry and group opportunities available at the warehouse or for a food drive.
Workforce DevelopmentVolunteers looking to assist with our workforce program can help by becoming a mentor/tutor for our financial literacy class, can offer to supply a meal for any of our classes, or provide childcare services for the families that need to bring children with them. Individual and group opportunities available.
Seasonal/ Holiday The Holidays bring a great deal of volunteer opportunities around The Place. These offerings include: Thanksgiving food drive and food pantry serving, Holiday House Event, Gift of Prom, Back to School Backpacks, Hot meals for seniors on the Holidays and much more.
Home Projects The opportunities to volunteer at home are great for families with younger children that want to serve The Place. These can include: Hosting a coat drive, putting together baskets for the homebound seniors for holidays, collecting food for a food drive, and so much more!

Orange Duffel Bag Initiative Graduation:Celebrating 17 Students
This past weekend, we celebrated an incredible milestone! 17 students graduated from our Orange Duffel Bag Initiative (ODBI)!
Each student stood up and gave a final presentation, sharing their goals, what they’ve learned, and the steps they are taking toward their future. It was a powerful moment to see their growth, confidence, and determination on full display.Through the 12 weeks of ODBI, students build life skills like goal setting, decision making, and healthy coping strategies. They are challenged to think about their future and take real steps toward it. At graduation, you can truly see that transformation.
Each graduate received a certificate, an orange duffel bag, and a laptop to support their next steps in school, work, and life.These moments are more than a celebration, they are a reminder of what is possible when students are supported, encouraged, and equipped with the tools they need to succeed.

March 2026 Newsletter for The Place
Gift of Prom reached an exciting milestone this year as we served 98 students across Forsyth and Dawson counties - our largest number ever.
What began seven years ago as a small effort to ensure that every student can experience the joy of prom has grown significantly, from serving just 23 students in 2022 to 98 in 2026. This year’s record participation reflects both the growing need in our community and the generosity of our donors and volunteers who make this event possible.
Thanks to remarkable community support, our boutique was stocked more abundantly than ever.
This year we received donations of 254 dresses, 52 tuxedos and men’s formalwear pieces, 103 pairs of shoes, 118 pieces of jewelry, and 136 makeup items. Combined with our existing inventory, we began the event with over 500 dresses, giving every student a wide range of options and styles to choose from.The abundance also allowed us to share resources with partner agencies, including Blessed Hope, Epic Prom, and White County.
The heart of Gift of Prom is always found in the personal moments, and this year brought many. One volunteer, Charlene, described her experience as “the most rewarding” she has had, sharing how meaningful it was to help teens find outfits that made them smile with pride.Charlene also recounted a touching side story: after talking about Gift of Prom with a cashier she sees regularly at Publix, the cashier, Tandy, decided to volunteer as well, and the two ended up joyfully working the same shift. These small connections reflect the spirit of community that keeps the program growing.
Another volunteer, Jean from the Forsyth County Junior Service League, shared the story of a student who had never worn a dress to a dance before.After exploring several jewel-toned options and laughing with her mom through the process, the student found a black dress that made her feel confident and beautiful. Even then, she hesitated, worried about taking something someone else might want.Jean encouraged her to choose what made her feel special, reminding her that she was the focus of the day. The student ultimately selected the dress along with jewelry and a vibrant red purse, leaving with a smile that Jean described as absolutely unforgettable.
These stories, paired with the dedication of volunteers, logistics team, staff, and the extraordinary generosity of donors, are what make Gift of Prom so impactful. Beyond providing dresses and suits, the program gives students memories of being celebrated, valued, and supported.Thank you to everyone who contributed time, resources, or care to make this year the most successful Gift of Prom yet.Your support truly changes lives and creates lasting moments these students will carry with them far beyond prom night.

What does real, lasting change look like?
In our newest podcast episode, we sit down with Meghan Livingston, our Case Management Manager at The Place, to talk about our Long-Term Case Management Program. This powerful program is made possible through a state grant and the generous support of community donors and partners like you.
Through this program, we walk closely with families for an extended period of time as they work toward self-sustainability. Participants commit to meeting one-on-one with staff and attending adult education classes, including financial literacy classes. Together, we create a plan for stability. Along the way, we can help with rent, deposits, utilities, and other urgent expenses, removing barriers while families build the skills and confidence they need for long-term success.
This is not just short-term assistance. This is relationship-based support that helps families stay housed, grow stronger, and move forward with hope.
Right now, you can help make this life-changing work possible through our Have a Heart for Our Community matching gift campaign through the Community Foundation for Northeast Georgia. Every gift brings us closer to unlocking our matching grant to increase your impact. Your support helps keep neighbors in homes while they work toward a stable future.

title: Summer Hunger Is Real. Together, We Can Make a Difference — The Place
text:
Summer Hunger Is Real. Together, We Can Make a Difference
Summer is a season of sunshine, family vacations, and children enjoying a well-deserved break from school. But for many families in our community, summer also brings a difficult reality: when school is out, access to regular, nutritious meals becomes much harder.
For many children, school breakfast and lunch programs provide consistent, healthy meals during the school year. Children can miss up to 10 meals per week during the summer months. When those meals are no longer available, parents and caregivers are left trying to stretch already limited grocery budgets to cover additional meals every day.
At The Place, we see this need firsthand. Throughout the summer, more families turn to our pantry for help because they simply need a little extra support to keep healthy food on the table.
Every child deserves a summer filled with fun, friendships, and opportunities to grow - not the uncertainty of wondering where their next meal will come from.
That's why our mission doesn't take a summer vacation.
Every week, generous donors, dedicated volunteers, and caring community partners help us provide food to children, families, seniors, and neighbors facing food insecurity. Their kindness allows us to offer hope along with every bag of groceries distributed.
But we can't do it alone.

Caring for our Homebound Seniors: Supporting Comfort, Dignity, and Connection
As our loved one’s age, many seniors face challenges that make it difficult to leave home independently. Illness, mobility limitations, chronic conditions, or recovery from surgery can all contribute to someone becoming homebound. While remaining at home often provides comfort and familiarity, it can also create feelings of isolation and make daily tasks more difficult.
Caring for homebound seniors requires a strong support system. This is where The Place can provide some much-neededconnection they need.
The Importance of Social Connection
One of the greatest challenges homebound seniors face is loneliness. Limited mobility can make it harder to stay connected with family, friends, and the community. Regular visits and phone calls can help seniors feel valued and less isolated. The Place offers an opportunity for connection with calls, food delivery, home repairs, and visits.
Creating a Safe and Comfortable Environment
Safety is a key part of caring for seniors at home. Making small adjustments can help prevent falls and injuries, such as:
Removing tripping hazards
Removing tripping hazards
Installing grab bars in bathrooms
Installing grab bars in bathrooms
Improving lighting throughout the home
Improving lighting throughout the home
Repairing loose or rotted handrails
Repairing loose or rotted handrails
Checking and installing new smoke detectors
Checking and installing new smoke detectors
The Place provides homebound seniors with services like home repairs, installing ramps, replacing broken windows, and much more to ensure they are safe in their own home.
How Volunteers Can Help
The Place is only able to offer these services to seniors because of the help of volunteers and community partners. Volunteers help by delivering meals, making phone calls, working on home projects, and more. To learn more about how you can help support the seniors in our community, please visit the Senior Assistance page.

Helping Our Kids Succeed
Youth Programs
School Snack Packs
Through our ongoing partnerships with school social workers and staff, we consistently hear that students who are hungry have a harder time focusing, participating, and staying engaged. Hunger affects attention, energy levels, and even behavior—especially later in the school day. School social workers have identified student snacks as one of the greatest unmet needs right now. Having access to reliable, nutritious snacks helps students stay regulated, attentive, and ready to learn, ensuring they can focus on what matters most: their education.
Holiday House
Holiday House is a heartwarming program that gives parents and guardians the dignity and joy of selecting new, unwrapped gifts their children truly want. Families facing hardships are invited to shop for their kids, choosing items that fit their needs and wishes.
Orange Duffel Bag Initiative
The Orange Duffel Bag Initiative is a 12-week program that empowers young people to identify their strengths, discover their purpose, set meaningful goals, and create a plan for their future through leadership development, self-discovery, and life-skills education.
Gift of Prom
Prom is a milestone that every student deserves the chance to enjoy. Through Gift of Prom, The Place helps under-resourced students participate in this special event by providing many of the items that can make prom financially out of reach. From dresses, shoes, and jewelry to tuxedo rentals, hair and makeup services, and other essentials, Gift of Prom helps remove barriers so students can celebrate this memorable occasion with confidence.
Graduation Gifts for McKinney-Vento Students
We close out the school year on an incredible high note, celebrating our McKinney‑Vento students with graduation gifts made possible through community generosity. The McKinney‑Vento Homeless Assistance Act ensures that children and youth experiencing homelessness have immediate school enrollment, educational stability, and transportation — removing barriers that often stand between them and academic success.
Summer Internships
The Summer Internship Program provides high school students with hands-on experience in community service and nonprofit work while helping them develop leadership, professional, and career-readiness skills through workshops, tours, projects, and volunteer experiences.

title: History — The Place
text:
The Place was founded in 1975 by four Dominican Nuns. The sisters offered assistance with financial needs, clothing, shelter, food, and even tutoring. Throughout our history, we have been the catalyst for several agencies that had their beginnings as programs at The Place.
In 2015, we started a workforce development initiative to help individuals who are unemployed or under-employed prepare for and secure jobs.
In 2021, we merged with Dawson County’s RIC-Rack thrift store and food pantry. We also implemented many of our current programs and services including financial assistance, workforce development and more.
Today, we serve our communities with emergency financial assistance, clothing, food, educational opportunities, plus numerous support services. Through our many initiatives and services, we are changing lives in Forsyth and Dawson counties of Georgia.

For five decades, neighbors have been helping neighbors. Today, your compassion continues that legacy.

Five Ways You Can Support The Place Year-Round
When most people think about giving back, they often think of the holidays. While the holiday season is an important time for nonprofits, the needs of our neighbors don't disappear once the decorations come down. Every day, families, seniors, and individuals in Forsyth and Dawson counties rely on The Place for food, financial assistance, education, workforce development, youth programs, and other essential services that help them move toward self-sufficiency.
Thanks to the generosity of our community, The Place has been serving local families for more than 50 years. Founded in 1975, our mission is simple yet powerful: to assist the people of Forsyth and Dawson County areas with essential needs and to be self-sustaining.
If you've been looking for meaningful ways to make an impact, here are five ways you can support The Place throughout the year.
1. Become a Monthly Donor
One of the most impactful ways to support The Place is by becoming a monthly donor through our Hearts of Impact giving program. Monthly gifts provide reliable funding that allows us to respond quickly to community needs, keep our food pantry shelves stocked, and invest in long-term programs that help individuals and families build brighter futures. Even a small recurring gift can create lasting change over time.
2. Volunteer Your Time
Volunteers are the heart of The Place. Whether you're sorting donations in our thrift store, helping distribute groceries, assisting with senior outreach, or serving at one of our special events, your time makes a direct difference in the lives of our neighbors. Whether you have a few hours each month or are looking for a regular volunteer opportunity, there's a place for everyone to serve.
3. Host a Donation or Food Drive
Looking for a way to involve your workplace, church, neighborhood, or civic organization? Hosting a food or donation drive is a fun and meaningful way to make a collective impact. The Place accepts donations of shelf-stable food, hygiene products, and other essential items that help us meet the growing needs of our community. Every donation helps ensure local families have access to the resources they need when they need them most.
4. Shop and Donate at The Place Thrift Store
Every purchase and every donated item at The Place Thrift Store helps fund programs and services that benefit our community. By shopping secondhand or donating gently used clothing, furniture, and household goods, you're giving items a second life while helping provide hope and opportunity for local families. It's a simple way to make a difference while supporting a mission you can feel good about.
5. Spread the Word
Not everyone can give financially—but everyone can help share our mission. Follow The Place on social media, share our posts, invite friends to volunteer, attend community events, or tell someone about the services we provide. Raising awareness helps connect more people to resources, recruit volunteers, and inspire others to give. Your voice can help expand our impact and ensure more neighbors know where to turn during difficult times.
Every Act of Kindness Matters
At The Place, we believe that strong communities are built when neighbors help neighbors. Whether you choose to donate, volunteer, shop, host a drive, or simply share our mission, your support helps provide food, stability, education, and hope to individuals and families throughout Forsyth and Dawson counties.
Together, we can continue to Support. Empower. Transform.—not just during the holidays, but every day of the year.

The Cottage: A Place to Find Stability, Build Confidence, and Create a Brighter Future
Every young woman deserves a safe place to call home. A place where she can feel supported, discover her strengths, set goals, and build a future she can be proud of. That is the heart behind The Cottage at The Place. The Cottage is a residence for goal-oriented young women ages 18–24 who are experiencing housing instability. More than simply providing a roof over someone’s head, The Cottage provides a safe, stable, and supportive home environment where young women can focus on what comes next.
Creating a Foundation for Independence
For a young woman experiencing housing instability, simply having a safe place to sleep can make an incredible difference. Stability creates an opportunity to focus on education, employment, personal goals, and the skills needed to live independently. At The Cottage, young women are encouraged to take ownership of their futures. With support and guidance, residents can develop the confidence and life skills they need to navigate adulthood and work toward self-sufficiency.
The goal is simple but powerful: to develop and empower confident, independent, self-sufficient young women.
More Than a Home
The Cottage is designed to be a place where young women feel safe, valued, and supported. It provides an environment where residents can establish routines, pursue their goals, and begin building the foundation for long-term stability.
What does that look like?
Continuing their education
Continuing their education
Employment
Employment
Learning to manage finances
Learning to manage finances
Developing healthy relationships
Developing healthy relationships
Preparing for independent living
Preparing for independent living
Under the guidance of a Case Management Manager and a Houseparent, these young women are given the tools they need to succeed.
“To me, The Cottage means a safe and long-term home. It provides me with the comfort I need to achieve my academic and professionals’ goals which allows me to build financial stability. The Cottage is more than a shelter; it is an opportunity to imagine and create the life you want. The loving and supportive people from The Cottage have helped me in more ways than any other assistance program, so I am grateful to call The Cottage my home,” – a Cottage resident.
How the Community Can Make a Difference
Programs like The Cottage are possible because of a community that believes every young person deserves the opportunity to thrive. Your support can help provide the resources, stability, and encouragement young women need as they work toward independence. Whether through a financial donation, providing needed supplies, or simply spreading the word about The Cottage, you can be part of creating brighter futures. Together, we can help ensure that young women experiencing housing instability don't have to navigate the journey alone.
The Cottage is more than a place to live. It is a place to grow, a place to dream, and a place to build a future.
At The Place, we believe in empowering young women to become confident, independent, and self-sufficient. We're grateful to have a community that believes in them, too.

Welcome to The Cottage!
A Place to Call Home. A Future to Call Her Own.
The Cottage was created for goal-oriented young women ages 18–24 who are experiencing housing instability, young women who have dreams for their future and are ready to work toward them, but may need a safe and stable place to begin.
At The Cottage, a safe home is just the beginning. Residents are supported as they pursue education, build careers, develop life skills, and work toward becoming independent and self-sufficient. And success looks different for every young woman. Sometimes it looks like starting a new job. Sometimes it's learning a new skill, preparing for independent living, or simply having a safe place to come home to at the end of the day.
And sometimes, it looks like walking across a stage to receive a college diploma.
On May 14, 2026, we had the incredible privilege of celebrating M as she graduated from the University of North Georgia with her bachelor's degree in Pre-Law, one full year ahead of schedule!
M has been part of The Cottage since high school, and watching her grow into the determined, intelligent, and resilient young woman she is today has been one of the great joys of this program.
Her graduation was more than an academic accomplishment. It was a celebration of how far she has come and the bright future ahead of her.
And M isn't the only one moving forward.
This summer, one Cottage resident began a teaching position with the Alliance Theatre and earned her Red Cross CPR and First Aid certification. Another is returning to work with Northside Hospital, while others continue to thrive in their careers and take important steps toward independence.
This is what The Cottage makes possible.
A safe and stable home gives these young women the space to focus on their goals, build confidence, develop life skills, and prepare for the future they want.
And you can help make that future possible.
When you support The Cottage, you're not simply helping provide a place to live. You're helping create the stability that allows a young woman to stay in school, pursue a career, learn to live independently, and believe in what comes next.
You might be helping provide the essentials that make a new room feel like home. You might be supporting the resources that help a resident reach her next goal. Or you might simply be part of the community standing behind her and reminding her that she doesn't have to build her future alone.

The Cottage Provides Young Women Facing Housing Insecurity with a Path to Stability and Success
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Jennifer Raaths, Communications Coordinatorjraaths@theplacega.org770-887-1098 x 236
August 19, 2026
The Cottage Provides Young Women Facing Housing Insecurity with a Path to Stability and Success
FORSYTH COUNTY, GA - In Forsyth County, young women ages 18-24 who are facing housing insecurity have a place to find stability, support, and the opportunity to build a brighter future. The Cottage, a group home established by The Place in 2021, provides a safe, supportive environment where young women can work toward independence, pursue their goals, and build successful futures.
The Cottage was created to meet the needs of goal-oriented young women, including those who have aged out of foster care and may be at risk of homelessness or housing instability. Through The Cottage, residents receive more than a place to live. They receive the guidance, resources, and support needed to take the next steps toward independence.
Each resident works closely with a Case Management Manager, House Parent, and additional support staff at The Place to develop an individualized plan and set defined goals for her future. From education and employment to financial stability and independent living skills, residents are encouraged and supported as they work toward becoming confident, self-sufficient young women.
"This is a long-term investment in a young woman who has defined goals," said Paige Whalen, Director of Client Services at The Place. "We work with young women to launch them successfully. We remove any barrier such as paying for housing, food or counseling so the women can focus solely on their educational and employment goals."
Since opening its doors in 2021, The Cottage has already helped seven residents graduate from college or vocational school - an achievement that demonstrates the impact of providing young women with stability and the resources they need to succeed.
"To me, The Cottage means a safe and long-term home. It provides me with the comfort I need to achieve my academic and professionals' goals which allows me to build financial stability. The Cottage is more than a shelter; it is an opportunity to imagine and create the life you want. The loving and supportive people from The Cottage have helped me in more ways than any other assistance program, so I am grateful to call The Cottage my home," - a Cottage resident.
The Cottage works with each resident to establish an individualized plan for success, helping her identify goals, overcome barriers, and develop the skills necessary for life beyond The Cottage. The goal is not simply to provide housing, but to create a foundation from which each young woman can build a stable, independent, and fulfilling future.
The Cottage is more than a home. It is a place where young women can find stability, discover their potential, and take meaningful steps toward a brighter future.
About The Place
The Place is a nonprofit organization dedicated to supporting individuals and families in Forsyth and Dawson counties by providing essential resources, career coaching, and community programs to help them achieve self-sufficiency.

The Place Honors Precision Concrete Construction With Community Partnership Award
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Contact:Nicole MorganThe Placenicole@theplacega.org | 770-887-1098 x242theplacega.org
The Place Honors Precision Concrete Construction With Community Partnership Award
Cumming, GA (November 2025) - The Place is proud to present Precision Concrete Construction with its Community Partnership Award in recognition of the company's extraordinary generosity, craftsmanship, and commitment to supporting vulnerable youth and families across Forsyth and Dawson counties.
Precision Concrete led a series of transformational projects for The Place, including major improvements to The Cottage, The Place's home for young women at risk of homelessness. The company donated significant labor, materials, supervision, and expertise to build a new driveway for The Cottage, ensuring safe access for residents, staff, and emergency services.
In addition to their work at The Cottage, Precision Concrete also completed key projects at The Place's main campus, including concrete enhancements for the thrift store drop-off area and a concrete pad for the organization's new outdoor walk-in freezer, which supports expanded food storage for the Food Pantry.
These projects represent a combined investment of more than $50,000, with Precision Concrete contributing the majority of the labor and coordination at no cost. The company also brought several partners to the table, whose donated or reduced-cost services helped make the work possible:
Grogan Disposal - Dumpster services
Grogan Disposal - Dumpster services
Argos Concrete - Donated concrete
Argos Concrete - Donated concrete
Contractors Sales International - Formwork materials and equipment
Contractors Sales International - Formwork materials and equipment
"Precision Concrete Construction stepped forward in a remarkable way," said Paige Whalen, Director of Client Services. "Their generosity has made our programs safer, stronger, and more accessible, especially for the young women living at The Cottage. This is what true community partnership looks like."
Jim Newsome, Vice President and Director of Construction Management at Precision Concrete, coordinated the projects and expressed the company's ongoing commitment to service. "We're glad we could help," leadership at Precision shared. "Please let us know how we can continue to support future projects this year."
The Place is grateful for Precision Concrete's leadership and for the outstanding community partners who joined them in their mission to serve neighbors in need.
About The Place
Since 1975, The Place has provided essential needs and support to families and individuals in Forsyth and Dawson counties, helping them become self-sustaining and stable. Through programs such as the Food Pantry, workforce development, youth initiatives, and The Cottage, The Place offers hope and practical help to neighbors in need.

The Place Hosts "Heartsgiving" to Support Local Families in Need
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Contact:Nicole MorganThe Placenicole@theplacega.org | 770-887-1098 x242theplacega.org
The Place Hosts "Heartsgiving" to Support Local Families in Need
Cumming, GA (October 24, 2025) - This November, The Place will host its first-ever Heartsgiving, a special event bringing warmth, food, and hope to families in need across Forsyth and Dawson counties.
Taking place November 18-20 in Forsyth County and November 20-21 in Dawson County, Heartsgiving will serve more than 450 families who receive assistance through The Place's Food Pantry. Each family will be able to select one coat per family member, receive a turkey, a box of food to complete their holiday meal, and a $25 gift card to help make their Thanksgiving brighter.
"This time of year can be especially hard for families already struggling to make ends meet," said Nicole Morgan, Director of Development The Place. "Heartsgiving is about more than just food and coats, it's about letting our neighbors know they are not alone. Together, we can make sure every family has a reason to give thanks."
The Place is inviting the community to join in spreading the spirit of giving through donations, sponsorships, and volunteer opportunities. The organization is currently collecting whole turkeys or turkey breasts, new or gently used coats, and monetary donations to help purchase food and supplies. Sponsors are also needed to help cover event expenses, and volunteers are welcome to help keep coats organized and racks full during the event.
Heartsgiving is made possible through community support and partnerships, including the PWB Joy of Hope Foundation.
"As the need continues to grow, so does our commitment to serve," added Morgan. "We've seen an increase in requests for help this year, and we're counting on our community's generosity to meet that need."
Those interested in donating, sponsoring, or volunteering can visit https://www.theplacega.org/heartsgiving for more information.

The Place's 11th Annual Holiday House Brings Dignity and Joy to Local Families
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Contact:Nicole MorganThe Placenicole@theplacega.org | 770-887-1098 x242theplacega.org/holidayhouse
The Place's 11th Annual Holiday House Brings Dignity and Joy to Local Families
Cumming, GA (November 2025) - The Place is celebrating the season of giving with its 11th Annual Holiday House, a cherished program that empowers parents and guardians facing financial hardship to personally select new gifts for their children, bringing dignity, joy, and hope to hundreds of families across Forsyth County.
Unlike traditional toy drives or giveaways, Holiday House uses a client-choice model that transforms the gift-giving experience. Families shop for their children in age-specific "toy shops" filled with community-donated toys, specialty items, and $25 gift cards (Target, Amazon, Ulta). Volunteers help them shop for the presents and prepare for the holidays, allowing parents to give gifts with love and pride.
"This event is truly special because it restores a sense of normalcy and dignity to families during a stressful time," said Paige Whalen, Director of Client Assistance at The Place. "Parents know their children best, what they like, what they need, and at Holiday House, they get to make those choices themselves. The impact goes far beyond the gifts."
In 2024, over 2,000 children received gifts through Holiday House, thanks to the generosity of sponsors, toy drives, and community volunteers. With requests for help continuing to rise this year, The Place expects even more families to register for assistance.
The Place is now seeking toy donations, $25 gift cards, event sponsors, and volunteers to help stock and staff Holiday House. New, unwrapped toys for children of all ages, especially teens, can be donated through December 5 at designated drop-off sites, or directly through give.theplacega.org/HolidayHouse or by visiting our Amazon wish list at https://linktr.ee/theplacega.hh
Businesses and organizations can also get involved by hosting toy drives, becoming sponsors, or volunteering during the event, which takes place December 10-13. Sponsorship opportunities start at $750, with all proceeds helping The Place purchase remaining toys and supplies needed to meet the growing demand.
"Our community's support makes Holiday House possible," added Whalen. "Every donation, every volunteer hour, every sponsor helps us create a season of joy - not just for children, but for their parents who get to experience the magic of giving."
About The Place
Since 1975, The Place of Forsyth County has provided essential needs and support to families and individuals in Forsyth and Dawson counties, helping them become self-sustaining and stable. Through programs such as the Food Pantry, workforce development, youth initiatives, and The Cottage, The Place offers hope and practical help to neighbors in need.

The Place's Holiday House Brings Joy, Dignity, and Hope to More Than 2,100 Children This Christmas Season
Forsyth County, GA - This holiday season, The Place once again brought the community together to ensure families could celebrate the holidays with joy, dignity, and hope through its 11th Annual Holiday House event.
Through Holiday House, 2,174 children from 860 families received brand-new, unwrapped toys, hand-selected by their parents or guardians. The event is designed to give caregivers the dignity and pleasure of choosing exactly what each child wants or needs for the holidays.
Holiday House is set up like a store, with toys organized by age group - Pre-School, Elementary, and Middle/High School - so families can easily find meaningful gifts for every child in their household.
